Found it. Commit 18f154d8 introduced this exact switch statement with the copy-paste bug (all cases using `Individual` properties) when the priority/flags system was first added.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 18f154d85110c36f6eb403d0a33703db4cfe8175

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I ran `git log --follow -p` on `XReservation.java` to trace its full history and located every commit that touched the file. I then inspected each candidate diff for the introduction of the `switch (type)` block seen in the fix.

**(2) Specific change:** Commit `18f154d8` (2014-12-05, "Tomáš Müller") is the commit that originally introduced `iPriority`/`iFlags` fields and the `switch (type)` block in the constructor. At that time, the `Group`, `Curriculum`, and `Course` cases were written by copy-pasting the `Individual` case block without updating the `ApplicationProperty` enum values (e.g., `ReservationPriorityIndividual` instead of `ReservationPriorityGroup`, etc.). This is a textbook copy-paste bug: all four case blocks (`Individual`, `Group`, `Curriculum`, `Course`) are byte-for-byte identical, using `*Individual` properties, when they should have used the type-specific properties as later corrected.

**(3) Evidence:** The diff of `18f154d8` shows the exact same buggy code (word-for-word, including the `ReservationPriorityIndividual`/`ReservationCanOverLimitIndividual`/etc. calls for `Group`, `Curriculum`, and `Course` cases) that the fixing commit `6eb8807d` later corrects to `*Group`, `*Curriculum`, and `*Course` respectively. No intervening commit modified this switch statement between `18f154d8` and the fix — the bug persisted unchanged from its introduction until it was fixed over a year later (Feb 2016).

I'm confident in this identification since the introduced code is an exact match to the pre-fix code in the bug-fixing diff.
